articles.title: Three key milestones on the road to financial freedom
articles.content: Financial freedom is built gradually through understanding, systematic investing and patience. articles.title: Dollar falls on surprise drop in US retail sales
articles.content: In July, US retail sales surprisingly took a dip, leading to a decline in the dollar's value. This drop enabled the euro and sterling to soar to their highest levels in months against the greenback. Additionally, softer inflation indicators have lowered the market's expectations for a potential rate hike by the Federal Reserve in September, raising alarms about the labor market following the payrolls report.

articles.title: Gold rises on weaker dollar as inflation data cements rate-hold bets
articles.content: On Friday, gold prices moved upward, signaling a positive outlook for the week. The precious metal received a boost from a weaker dollar and stable inflation figures, reducing the likelihood of an upcoming interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. Meanwhile, oil prices also showed weekly gains, influenced by escalating tensions in the Strait of Hormuz. Precious metals such as silver and platinum followed suit, while palladium experienced a decline.

articles.title: Oil inches toward $90 on tanker attacks, lack of progress in Iran war peace deal
articles.content: Crude oil futures experienced an upward trend on Friday due to disruptions from tanker attacks and the stagnation of peace talks. Brent crude closed at $88.52 a barrel while WTI crude settled at $82.40. Attacks within the Strait of Hormuz and disruptions at a Russian port led to a decline in shipping activity. Fortunately, storage levels have proven more resilient, potentially exerting downward pressure on prices.

articles.title: Alphabet becomes Berkshire Hathaway's third-largest investment
articles.content: In the second quarter, Berkshire Hathaway raised its investment in Alphabet by a significant eighty-three percent, positioning it as the company's third-largest holding, following Apple and American Express. The firm also diminished its cash reserves and ceased a prolonged selling trend. Additionally, investments in Delta Air Lines and Macy's saw increases, while Constellation Brands was removed from the portfolio, as outlined in a recent regulatory filing.

articles.title: European shares snap 4-week rally as higher oil prices temper strong earnings
articles.content: European stock markets closed in the red on Friday, breaking a four-week winning streak. The rise in crude oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions overshadowed robust corporate earnings. Although the STOXX 600 index experienced a weekly decline, it remained close to record levels, buoyed by strong economic growth and profits across sectors. Investors began reallocating their portfolios, moving away from stocks related to artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Anthropic IPO valuation hinges on $190-200 billion 2028 revenue forecast, sources say
articles.content: As Anthropic prepares for its initial public offering, Wall Street is keenly evaluating the company's worth through the lens of its projected revenue growth, expected to soar by 2028. This outlook is crucial, leading investors to utilize enterprise value-to-revenue multiples derived from forecasted figures. Benchmarking against industry players like Palantir and SpaceX highlights both the promising future and the infrastructural challenges facing Anthropic.

articles.title: Institutional investors reveal cautious approach to tech favorites in US quarterly 13F filings
articles.content: In the second quarter, institutional investors made slight reductions in their holdings of prominent tech firms, mainly due to already substantial positions making further investments challenging. However, semiconductor stocks continued to attract a positive outlook, while AI-themed stocks saw a decline in traction after an initial wave of interest. Interestingly, the energy sector faced more selling than buying activity during this period.

articles.title: SEC proposes easing 'pay-to-play' rules for investment advisers
articles.content: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is looking to relax rules that prevent investment advisers from managing public pension funds due to political contributions. These proposed amendments are intended to alleviate the compliance challenges faced by advisers and address longstanding issues raised by various political factions. Regulators are now inviting stakeholder feedback on these significant regulatory changes.
